UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


Southwest Power Pool, Inc.                               )                               Docket No. ER26-1323-000


                       LIMITED PROTEST OF ENCHANTED ROCK, LLC

         Pursuant to Rules 2111 and 2122 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

(“Commission” or “FERC”)’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, Enchanted Rock, LLC

(“Enchanted Rock”)3 hereby files this limited protest (“Protest”) of Southwest Power Pool, Inc.’s

(“SPP”) proposed revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”)4 submitted in the

captioned proceeding,5 to add Conditional High Impact Large Load Service6 (“CHILLS”) that

will allow High Impact Large Loads (“HILLs”) to be served with non-firm conditional

transmission service.7 While Enchanted Rock is generally supportive of the CHILLS Proposal

and SPP’s goal of “mitigat[ing] the challenges of integrating HILLs into the Transmission

System,”8 SPP has failed to meet its burden under Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)

to demonstrate that the CHILLS Proposal, as filed, is just and reasonable.9 This is because SPP

grid.

 has proposed tariff revisions applicable during Emergency Conditions and other specified

circumstances (referred to herein as the “Emergency Override Provisions”10), that would not

only eliminate a CHILLS Customer’s11 impact on the grid by dispatching its supporting High

Impact Large Load Generation Assessment resource (the “HILLGA Resource”), but would also

further curtail the CHILLS Customer’s load to create a net injection from the HILLGA Resource

that remains online. As discussed further herein, the Emergency Override Provisions undermine

the core purpose of CHILLS, as well as the broader HILL/HILLGA market framework, because,

inter alia, the Emergency Override Provisions will dissuade HILLs from adopting CHILLS

because HILLs will not be able to rely on their HILLGA Resource to serve it during Emergency

Conditions, and will impose unjustified costs on CHILLS Customers. In turn, the Emergency

Override Provisions will delay the effective integration of HILLs into the SPP market and will

not support the United States’ national interests and goals of maintaining dominance in the field

of Artificial Intelligence (“AI”)12 and reshoring manufacturing.13

        Accordingly, for these reasons, and the reasons discussed further herein, Enchanted Rock

respectfully requests that the Commission reject the CHILLS Proposal without prejudice, and

Proposed Tariff Attachment AE, Section 2.22.2(2)(b) are underlined below:

        Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service as defined in Attachment BB of the
        Tariff must . . . (b) Ensure the sum of the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limits of
        supporting Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service, as defined in
        Attachment BB of the Tariff, does not exceed the submitted HILL or CHILL load forecast value of
        the corresponding HILL or CHILL except when directed by the Transmission Provider to mitigate
        Emergency Conditions or as specified in the Resource’s generator interconnection agreement.
11
   A HILL electing CHILLS shall sometimes be referred to herein as a “CHILLS Customer.”
12
   See CHILLS Filing Letter at 2 (“In 2025, the Trump Administration announced that ‘[i]t is the policy of the
United States to sustain and enhance America's global AI dominance in order to promote human flourishing,
economic competitiveness, and national security.’”) (citing Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial
Intelligence, Executive Order 14179, 90 FR 8741 (Jan. 23, 2025)).
13
   See CHILLS Filing Letter at 2 (citing Regulatory Relief to Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines,
Executive Order 14293, 90 FR 19615 (May 5, 2025)).


                                                        2
 direct SPP to refile the CHILLS Proposal with the Emergency Override Provisions removed.

Alternatively, if the Commission accepts the CHILLS Proposal as filed, Enchanted Rock

respectfully requests that the Commission direct SPP and its stakeholders to consider additional

changes to the SPP Tariff to address the concerns raised by Enchanted Rock herein related to the

Emergency Override Provisions.

     I.        PROTEST

          A.     The Emergency Override Provisions Render the CHILLS Proposal Unjust and
                 Unreasonable

          Enchanted Rock supports SPP’s proposed introduction of a non-firm, as-available,

interruptible transmission service such as CHILLS to enable faster interconnection of HILLs —

including AI data centers and other mission critical facilities—in a resource-constrained

environment.14 Further, Enchanted Rock supported SPP’s recently-accepted proposal related to

HILLs and the HILLGA process,15 which “facilitates the prompt interconnection of generating

resources that are specifically identified for and limited to serving a HILL.”16 Enchanted Rock

also supports the CHILL Proposal’s core requirement that a HILL needs to have supporting

generation in commercial operation prior to the HILL being eligible to take CHILLS17 given the

critical importance of having dedicated Resources in place to serve the HILL. Moreover,

Enchanted Rock is supportive of the CHILLS Proposal’s requirement that Resources with Load

Limited Resource Interconnection Service (“LLRIS”) must generally “[e]nsure the sum of the

Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limits of supporting Resources with Load Limited




14
   See, e.g., CHILLS Filing Letter at 14-15.
15
   See, generally, Comments of Enchanted Rock, LLC, Docket No. ER26-247-000 (Nov. 14, 2025).
16
   See CHILLS Filing Letter at 7 (emphasis added).
17
   See, e.g., id. at 21.


                                                     3
 Resource Interconnection Service, as defined in Attachment BB of the Tariff, does not exceed the

submitted HILL or CHILL load forecast value of the corresponding HILL or CHILL . . . .”18

        Notwithstanding the foregoing, Commission acceptance of the CHILLS Proposal

pursuant to FPA Section 205 is not warranted due to the proposed Emergency Override

Provisions. These provisions require that the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limits of

supporting Resources with LLRIS (i.e., HILLGA Resources) may exceed the submitted HILL or

CHILL load forecast value of the corresponding HILL or CHILL “when directed by the

Transmission Provider to mitigate Emergency Conditions or as specified in the Resource’s

generator interconnection agreement.”19 The ability for SPP to call on a HILLGA Resource to

serve the needs of the SPP market and be dispatched higher by SPP if needed to mitigate

Emergency Conditions,20 have not been demonstrated to be just and reasonable by SPP for the

reasons discussed in further detail below.

                 i.       The Emergency Override Provisions Undermine a Fundamental Purpose
                          of CHILLS

        As noted, CHILLS is explicitly designed as a non-firm, interruptible transmission service,

and it is reasonable for such service to be subject to curtailment to prioritize firm loads and

higher priority services during transmission constraints, local reliability issues, or broader system

conditions.21 Enchanted Rock fully supports this curtailment priority to avoid disruption to other

customers, including residential customers, as it reflects conditions that CHILLS Customers

knowingly accept when electing to utilize a more expedited, non-firm transmission option.

However, the Emergency Override Provisions, which allow SPP to curtail CHILLS Customers



18
   See Proposed Tariff Attachment AE, Section 2.22.2(2)(b).
19
   See id.
20
   See CHILLS Filing Letter at 35.
21
   See, e.g., id. at 14-15.


                                                        4
 while simultaneously directing the supporting HILLGA Resource (interconnected via LLRIS) to

be dispatched to serve the broader market during Emergency Conditions (or merely when

permitted by such Resource’s generator interconnection agreement), result in CHILLS

Customers – which are taking a temporary, interim transmission service22 – providing twice their

curtailment value to the grid during Emergency Conditions. That is, CHILLS Customers first

can have their HILLGA Resource dispatched to remove the CHILLS Customer’s impact on the

transmission system, and then have their load curtailed during Emergency Conditions while the

HILLGA Resource serves the broader SPP market rather than the CHILLS Customer. This

construct does not align with current, standard industry practices, where large load customers

rely on backup generation to continue their own operations during emergencies when they are

curtailed by grid operators, but the backup generation itself is not required to export power to the

grid while the large load is curtailed, which would leave the large load customer exposed to the

risk of going completely offline.

        The Emergency Override Provisions thus undermine a fundamental purpose of the overall

CHILLS and the HILL/HILLGA framework. Specifically, SPP established LLRIS to “facilitate

the prompt interconnection of generating Resources that are specifically identified for and

limited to serving a HILL [i.e., the HILLGA Resource],”23 and noted that “LLRIS is limited

interconnection service that allows the HILLGA Customer to integrate its Generating Facility

with the Transmission System with injection rights limited to the HILL, which it is supporting.”24

Moreover, SPP stated that “LLRIS grants limited interconnection rights solely to support the




22
   See, e.g., id. at 14 (noting CHILLS is available for up to a maximum of seven years).
23
   See Submission of Tariff Revisions to Add the High Impact Large Load Processes and High Impact Large Load
Generation Assessment, Docket No. ER26-247-000, at 23 (Oct. 25, 2026).
24
   See id.


                                                      5
 HILL . . . .”25 LLRIS, and the associated HILLGA Resource, thus facilitate reliable power to

support a CHILLS Customer even when the transmission system is constrained or unavailable,

thereby enabling the CHILLS Customer to avoid total shutdowns or complete loss of service

when the CHILLS Customer is curtailed by SPP due to system conditions. A fundamental

purpose of the CHILLS framework is to ensure that, during transmission constraints or

emergencies, the supporting HILLGA Resource remains available to serve the curtailed CHILLS

Customer, allowing the CHILLS Customer to continue meeting its own power needs from its

dedicated generation rather than face the risk of a total shutdown. This proposed market design

and reliability construct is critical to ensure that HILLs will elect to utilize CHILLS, as HILLs

(particularly AI data centers) generally do not tolerate the risk of being completely offline for any

material amount of time, meaning that they will need an alternative source of power even if

curtailed by SPP.

           Unfortunately, the proposed Emergency Override Provisions cause SPP’s entire proposed

market and reliability construct to collapse at the very moment it is most needed—during

Emergency Conditions. Accordingly, the Emergency Override Provisions expose the CHILLS

Customer to total loss of power any time when circumstances are “imminently likely to cause a

material adverse effect on the security of, or damage to the Transmission System.” 26 In practice,

this will mean that it is a near certainty that HILLs will be unable to rely solely on HILLGA

Resources to serve them during Emergency Conditions, which will disincentive HILLS from

utilizing CHILLS at all.




25
     See id. at 29 (emphasis added).
26
     See SPP Tariff, Part I, Section 1, Definition of Emergency Condition.


                                                            6
         The Emergency Override Provisions thus undermine the central objective of the CHILLS

Proposal (i.e., encouraging the use of CHILLS), which in turn means that SPP has failed to meet

its burden under FPA Section 205 to justify Commission acceptance of the CHILLS Proposal.27

                 ii.      The Emergency Override Provisions Result in Unjust, Unreasonable and
                          Unduly Discriminatory Cost Increases and Will Exacerbate Fuel-Related
                          Challenges

        In the alternative, even if some HILLs do elect to utilize CHILLS, they will almost

certainly need to develop, permit, and maintain separate emergency backup generation (e.g., gas

turbines, diesel back-up, battery systems, etc.) sized for the HILL’s full capacity to ensure

reliable operations during Emergency Conditions because the (not so) dedicated HILLGA

Resource may be redirected to serve the SPP market during Emergency Conditions, while the

CHILLS Customer could simultaneously be curtailed. This paradigm will almost certainly force

CHILLS Customers to procure separate and additional backup generation systems to achieve the

reliability they need and will require the CHILLS Customer to procure firm fuel transportation

rights for both the HILLGA Resource and the additional backup generation. These additional

costs are wholly unnecessary and excessive and due solely to the Emergency Override

Provisions, and therefore, SPP has failed to show how the Emergency Override Provisions are

just and reasonable pursuant to FPA Section 205.28

         Further, in the event that the HILL uses natural gas for the HILLGA Resource and its

backup generation, the HILL’s need to secure natural gas transportation rights for such a large

load will unnecessarily drive up reservation fees, exacerbate shortages, and potentially limit fuel



27
   See, e.g., PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 175 FERC ¶ 61,084 (2021) (rejecting an FPA Section 205 filing as unjust
and unreasonable where the proposed tariff changes did not achieve PJM’s stated reliability objective and therefore
failed to accomplish its purpose); NRG Power Mktg., LLC v. FERC, 430 U.S. App. D.C. 224, 226, 862 F.3d 108, 110
(2017) (noting that FERC cannot accept a proposal that results in a fundamentally different rate design than what
was proposed, particularly if it fails to resolve the issues it aimed to address).
28
   See, e.g., 16 U.S.C. § 824d(a).


                                                        7
 availability for other power generators, industrial users, and residential/commercial customers

given the already constrained firm natural gas pipeline capacity in SPP.29 If the emergency

backup generation is instead diesel-fired, which is a common alternative to natural gas, diesel

fuel supply chains are highly vulnerable during crises, with limited storage, just-in-time delivery

logistics, and historic shortages during extreme weather events or widespread grid emergencies.30

Requiring a CHILLS Customer to have such a large diesel backup fleet would require the

CHILLS Customer to stockpile or secure priority access to large volumes of diesel fuel on-site or

via dedicated contracts, pulling significant quantities away from other end-users—such as

hospitals, emergency services, trucking, agriculture, and residential heating—that rely on diesel

during the same high-stress periods. This unnecessary diversion of finite diesel resources during

crises can constrain availability for those other critical customers, increase spot-market prices,

and heighten regional fuel supply risks.

         Accordingly, in addition to unnecessarily increasing costs on CHILLS Customers, the

Emergency Override Provisions, if adopted, will likely unnecessarily constrain and burden

natural gas and/or diesel fuel supplies, resulting in negative economic and reliability-related

impacts to other customers. For these additional reasons, the Commission should reject the

CHILLS Proposal, as filed.31



29
   See, e.g., North American Electric Reliability Corporation, 2025 Long Term Reliability Assessment, at 35-36 (Jan.
23, 2026), (noting that in regions adding significant natural gas resources, including SPP, generators “will need to
compete with other pipeline customers for firm supply and delivery during periods of high gas demand”), available
at: https://www.nerc.com/globalassets/our-work/assessments/nerc_ltra_2025.pdf.
30
   See, e.g., National Renewable Energy Laboratory, A Comparison of Fuel Choice for Backup Generators, at 10
(noting that “resupply shipments to diesel generators during extreme weather events are common but far from
guaranteed”), available at: https://docs.nrel.gov/docs/fy19osti/72509.pdf.
31
   Additionally, when both the HILLGA Resource and the required emergency backup generation (diesel or gas-
fired) are installed at the same site, the combined potential-to-emit (“PTE”) from these generation resources risk
pushing the large load facility towards major source thresholds under the Clean Air Act’s Title V program pursuant
to 40 C.F.R. Part 70. This, in turn, can cause the large load facility to face significant operational challenges.




                                                         8
        B.      Requested Relief

       For the reasons discussed herein, Enchanted Rock respectfully requests that the

Commission reject the CHILLS Proposal without prejudice, and direct SPP to refile the CHILLS

Proposal with the Emergency Override Provisions removed. Specifically, Enchanted Rock

requests that SPP refile the CHILLS Proposal, but with the following revisions to Proposed

Tariff Attachment AE, Section 2.22.2(2)(b):

       Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service as defined in
       Attachment BB of the Tariff must . . .

       (b) Ensure the sum of the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limits of
       supporting Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service, as
       defined in Attachment BB of the Tariff, does not exceed the submitted HILL or
       CHILL load forecast value of the corresponding HILL or CHILL except when
       directed by the Transmission Provider to mitigate Emergency Conditions or as
       specified in the Resource’s generator interconnection agreement.

       Alternatively, if the Commission accepts the CHILLS Proposal as filed, Enchanted Rock

respectfully requests that the Commission direct SPP and its stakeholders to consider additional

changes to the SPP Tariff to address the concerns raised by Enchanted Rock herein related to the

Emergency Override Provisions.




                                                9
 II.    CONCLUSION

       For the foregoing reasons, Enchanted Rock respectfully requests that the Commission

consider this Protest, and grant the relief requested herein.
